_comment: 🔮️ Test-only references of the quiz product (Protocol v2). Every case under ../🧪️tests names one of these oracles; the TypeScript twin (@semio-tech/quiz) and the Rust twin (semio-framework-quiz) are the subjects and are additionally held to each other. The Python references live inside the case adapters (🧪️tests/*/🐍️.py) and are written from the design text only. Shared vectors under ../🧫️fixtures are generated from those same adapters, so a committed vector and its oracle can never disagree; the generation command is stated in every feature.

oracles.rationale: The quiz randomness contract (design §3) is MT19937 seeded with init_genrand and read as tempered u32 words, plus FNV-1a seeds, rejection-sampled uniform indices and a Fisher–Yates shuffle over that stream. numpy's MT19937 bit generator is the reference stream: RandomState(seed) runs init_genrand for a scalar seed and the state is handed to MT19937.random_raw unchanged. The case additionally loads CPython's own random.Random — an unrelated MT19937 implementation — with the same 624-word state and requires the same words, and pins the C++ standard's check value (the 10000th word of a default-seeded std::mt19937 is 4123659995, [rand.predef]). Surveyed and declined: seedrandom (ARC4/xor families, no MT19937), pure-rand (its MT19937 is not exposed as raw tempered words with init_genrand seeding across versions), jstat (no PRNG). FNV-1a, uniform and shuffle are derived in the adapter from the design text and consume only the library's words.

packages.role: Vectorised pair matrices (subtract.outer, greater.outer, sign) and pairwise summation for the weighted concordance cross-check.

oracles.rationale: Scoring (design §6) is a magnitude-weighted pair concordance for sorting and matching and a profile-distance credit for classification. No library implements the magnitude weights — they are this product's policy — so the oracle adapters compute the projected score with the design's pair loop and refuse to project it unless two independent evaluations agree within 1e-12: numpy over the full pair matrix (unrelated evaluation and summation order), and scipy.stats.kendalltau for the unit-weight reading of the same engine, where the score is (1 + τ_a)/2 over the pairs the truth orders and τ_a follows from scipy's τ_b and the tie counts. Classification distances and d_max are recomputed with scipy.spatial.distance.euclidean and pdist. Surveyed and declined: jstat (no Kendall τ with tie handling), simple-statistics (not in the lockfile, no tie-corrected τ_b).

The contract 🧬️schema/🔣️.json is JSON Schema draft-07 and normative; the product validates quizzes and catalogs with its own structural and semantic validator (quizIssues, catalogIssues) and deliberately links no schema library at runtime. python-jsonschema's Draft7Validator reads the normative file itself and judges every quiz and catalog the product meets — the committed vectors, the authored teaching content and a set of rejected documents that each break one named rule — so the owned validator is held to the schema rather than to its own reading of it. It also validates every other schema-typed document in the committed vectors (sheets, answers, results, commands, events, views) and fails the oracle phase on any violation. ajv (already in the lockfile) was the alternative; the Python host was chosen so the conformance oracle sits beside the other Python references of this owner.

packages.role: The MT19937 stream every sheet is drawn from.

engine.implementation: in-repository second implementation of design §3–§8, written in Python from the design text

oracles.rationale: Sheet assembly, answer validity, badge rules, the leaderboard's tie-break chain and the learner lifecycle are this product's own policy: no third party implements them, and a survey of the Python, JavaScript and Rust ecosystems (quiz engines such as H5P, Moodle's question engine and Open edX's capa problems score per question with their own rubrics and randomise with platform RNGs) found nothing that could state these outcomes. The reference is therefore a second implementation written in Python from the design text only, never from the TypeScript or Rust twins, drawing sheets from numpy's MT19937. It is registered as a cross-semio implementation — a supplement, never third-party evidence — and it is not the only check: both twins are also held to each other by the harness's pairwise subject parity, so every one of these cases compares three independently written readings of the design.

Judges the sorting score inside the unit suite `🧪️tests/⚖️partial-credit-scoring` of @semio-tech/quiz (vitest, devDependency of the core package). With equally spaced values on a linear scale the magnitude weights are rank differences, and the weighted pair concordance then equals (1 + ρ)/2 with Spearman's ρ — so jStat.spearmancoeff states the score of every permutation the suite draws (n = 2…15) within 1e-12. This is the rank reading of design §6; the Kendall reading with unit weights is judged by quiz-scipy-stats in the Protocol v2 case.

Judges the profile distances d and d_max of the classification credit inside the unit suite `🧪️tests/⚖️partial-credit-scoring` of @semio-tech/quiz (vitest, devDependency of the core package): math.distance over the normalised profiles must reproduce every distance the owned credit uses. scipy.spatial.distance is the corresponding reference of the Protocol v2 case (quiz-scipy-stats).

Judges the owned structural validator inside the unit suite `🧪️tests/🩺️document-validation` of @semio-tech/quiz (vitest, devDependency of the core package): ajv compiles the normative 🧬️schema/🔣️.json and, for every tested quiz and catalog document, accepts it exactly when quizIssues/catalogIssues report no structural issue. It is the JavaScript engine beside python-jsonschema (quiz-jsonschema), which judges the same contract in the Protocol v2 case — two independent schema engines.

Judges the owned radar (spider diagram) geometry of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🕷️radar-geometry` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): every axis value maps to its radius by d3-scale's scaleLinear with clamping over the axis [min, max], for 3 to 9 axes (252 points), and the owned renderer must place the same points. The renderer itself links no chart library.

Judges the owned radar label layout of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🕷️radar-geometry` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): opentype.js parses the site's brand font and measures real glyph advances, and every wrapped axis label box the owned renderer lays out must stay inside the chart at phone, tablet and desktop widths. The renderer itself measures with an owned width estimate and links no font library.

comparisonProfiles.description: Structural identity with the quiz scoring parity tolerance of 1e-12 (design §6): log10 may differ by one ulp between language runtimes. Ids, kinds, orders and every non-numeric field still compare exactly.

subjectFeatures.rationale: 🧪️ The quiz crate re-exports its JSON codec (serde_json) only under `sut`, so the Rust subject adapters can decode the shared vectors into the typed twins and encode their answers, while production builds of the crate stay free of it.

oracleHostPackages.rationale: 🌀️ MT19937 stream of the randomness oracle and of every Python reference that draws a sheet; pair matrices of the scoring cross-checks.
📊️ Kendall τ and Euclidean distances of the scoring cross-checks.
🧬️ Draft 7 validation of every quiz document against the normative schema.
